LESSON: SIGN READING 11.2.2 FLUENCY

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.2: Sign reading 11.2.2 Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign reading 11.2.2 Fluency, part of Strand 11 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three General.

Key inquiry question: Why it is important to sign read fluently?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign reading 11.2.2 Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: as the learner sign reads fluently.

• Collaboration: Teamwork is cultivated as the learner actively participates in a reader’s theatre with peers.

Values:
Respect is developed as the learner appreciates the effort of peers in sign reading fluently during a reader’s theatre.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (Self-esteem): The learner acquires a high level of self-esteem as they sign read fluently.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Fluency is applied when sign reading texts in class for information in all learning areas.

Suggested Learning Resources

Chart, Class readers, Adapted Course books, Flash cards, Recording devices e.g tablets, mobile phone, Dictionary, Internet, Audio-visual recordings,

Posters, Pictures and Photographs, Extracts from newspapers, magazines.
